item.title: 'Bigger than Barack Obama's election': Scholars reflect on Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Scott Colom is now this Southern state's first Black U.S. senator in nearly 150 years. Scholars and Mississippi natives Eddie Glaude and Kiese Laymon discuss the historic significance of his victory.
item.content:encoded: Scott Colom is now this Southern state's first Black U.S. senator in nearly 150 years. Scholars and Mississippi natives Eddie Glaude and Kiese Laymon discuss the historic significance of his victory.

item.title: The midterms were the largest win for either party in 50 years
item.description: Some 56% of people cast votes for Democrats in House races, compared to 42% who voted Republican. That 14-point spread is the widest win for either party in 50 years, since after Watergate.
item.content:encoded: Some 56% of people cast votes for Democrats in House races, compared to 42% who voted Republican. That 14-point spread is the widest win for either party in 50 years, since after Watergate.

item.title: The U.N.'s top court rules Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya
item.description: The International Court of Justice found that Myanmar security forces "acted with genocidal intent" against the Rohingya during military operations in the northern Rakhine state in 2017.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: The law releasing the Epstein files passed one year ago. What do his victims say?
item.description: It's been a year since the House passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, forcing the Justice Department to release millions of files connected to the convicted sex offender. His victims speak out.

item.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is a national security issue
item.description: The Nvidia scandal has spilled over into the Trump administration, which is now under intense scrutiny for how it allowed America's top AI chips to end up in China's hands.

item.title: Democrats nominate Jeffries for speaker, prep investigations into Trump's orbit
item.description: Democrats gave the official nod to Hakeem Jeffries to be the next speaker of the House. Meanwhile, Democrats are ramping up their plans to investigate the Trump administration come January.
